I'm a 46-year-old man farming 66 mu in Dongfu Village, Anzhai Township, Quzhou County. I only started farming 6 years ago — before that I worked in construction in Shijiazhuang. My middle school education means I can read labels and do basic math, but I still rely heavily on watching what my neighbors do. Six years isn't long enough to have seen every kind of year, so when something unusual happens, I get nervous.

My farm is a "family farm" at 66 mu — bigger than the smallholders around me, but I'm not running a big agribusiness either. I have my wife and one child still at home to help, plus I hire some seasonal labor when things get tight. I grow wheat-maize rotation on 36 mu, stevia on 10 mu, and sweet potato on 20 mu. The stevia and sweet potato are my cash crops — they pay better than grain, but they're also more work and riskier. The wheat-maize is my baseline. No matter what happens, I know I can sell grain, and my family needs flour and feed.

**Wheat (36 mu):** I plant around October 18th, right after National Day when the soil is still warm enough. I use a rotary tiller — it's fast and I've got the machinery. Seed rate is about 30 jin per mu, bought from the seed station. I used to try saving seed but the germination was inconsistent. For fertilizer, I put down about 100 jin of compound (the 18-22-5 blend) before sowing with the machine, then topdress another 40 jin of the high-nitrogen compound at jointing. That's what my neighbor Lao Zhang does on his wheat and he gets good tillering. I irrigate 3 times — winter irrigation from the well, then twice in spring. The water meter is expensive so I watch it, but last year I cut back to 2 times and the yield dropped to 900 jin/mu, which hurt. I spray insecticide once and herbicide once, usually around tillering. I'm expecting about 1000 jin (500 kg) per mu if the spring rain cooperates.

**Maize (36 mu, same fields):** This is the tight window — wheat comes off around June 7th and maize goes in immediately after. I don't till, just direct seed with the planter. I buy hybrid seed in packages, about 1 package per mu. I put down 80 jin of the 28-6-6 compound at planting. The extension agent says I should topdress urea at the big flare stage, but honestly with only 6 years experience, I find it hard to judge the timing, and last year I missed it and still got 1300 jin/mu. So this year I'm keeping it simple — basal fertilizer only. I irrigate twice, both in July-August when it's dry. Two insecticide sprays, one herbicide, and one growth regulator. Harvest by machine in early October. I'm hoping for 1300 jin (650 kg) per mu, maybe 1400 if the summer rains are good.

**Sweet Potato (20 mu):** This is my biggest gamble but also my best moneymaker. I plow deep — 350 yuan per mu for tractor plowing — because tubers need loose soil. I plant around April 2nd with cuttings I save from last year, about 4000 plants per mu. I broadcast urea (10 jin/mu), superphosphate (80 jin/mu), and potassium sulfate (30 jin/mu) before planting, then topdress with 15 jin of compound fertilizer later. The phosphate and potash are expensive but without them the tubers stay small and don't store well. I irrigate twice — sweet potato is drought-tolerant but the tuber filling stage needs water. I have to do a lot of hand weeding (31 hours per mu!) and spray insecticide 3 times. I also use growth regulator 3 times to control the vines. Harvest is late October, mostly by hand with some machine help. Last year I got 6000 kg/mu and sold at 0.75 yuan/kg. That's 4500 yuan per mu, which is why I keep growing it despite the labor.

**Stevia (10 mu):** This is a contract crop — the buyer comes to the village. I plant in early April and harvest in early September. I buy seedlings at 600 yuan per mu — they're expensive but you need good varieties for the sugar content. I put plastic film on the rows (5 jin per mu) to keep moisture and control weeds. Basal fertilizer is 100 jin of 15-15-15 compound, then I topdress twice with another 160 jin total of the same compound. I also spread 80 jin of organic manure at planting — stevia likes rich soil. This crop needs a lot of water — 4 irrigations — and a LOT of pesticide: 10 insecticide sprays, 1 herbicide, and 10 fungicide sprays. If leaf spot gets in, the whole contract is ruined. It's labor intensive (24 hours harvest labor per mu) but at 6.5 yuan/kg and 450 kg/mu yield, it brings in nearly 3000 yuan per mu. The problem is I'm locked into the buyer's price.

**Labor and cash:** My wife and I handle most of the day-to-day work. During wheat harvest and maize planting, we hire a combine and some helpers. Sweet potato harvest needs extra hands too. Total input costs this year will run about 45,000–47,000 yuan. That's a lot of money to spend before I see any income, and with only 6 years experience, I still get anxious writing those checks. But I've learned that under-investing costs more than over-investing — a bad year without enough fertilizer or water, and I'm eating into my savings. I'd rather spend a bit more and sleep better.
